body:
Narrative Codex review: canonical evidence view, derived page geometry

I support the Narrative Codex as a canonical view of the system. The important qualification is that the annotation-bearing source flow is canonical; page numbers, line breaks, and rectangles are derived presentation geometry.

C1 BLOCKING: separate semantic compilation from text layout.

The proposed contract StoryModel plus CodexViewSpec to AnnotatedPages currently makes a pure compiler responsible for font shaping, line breaking, pagination, and page fragment geometry. Those are not portable data operations. The contract should be split:

  StoryModel Validated plus CommonViewState plus CodexSpec
    to CodexFlow

  CodexFlow plus PaginationSpec plus TextLayoutCapability
    to PlacedCodex

CodexFlow contains exact source runs, stable annotations, spans, priorities, audit trails, and continuation policy. PlacedCodex contains pages, lines, rectangles, and annotation fragments. A browser adapter can produce PlacedCodex from live DOM geometry; a publication backend can use an owned deterministic paginator. This also makes continuous scroll and fixed edition mode two layouts of the same semantic artifact.

C2: Range.getClientRects is a good interactive adapter, not a pure or platform-independent compiler.

The CSSOM View specification defines range rectangles as runtime layout geometry, and FontFaceSet.ready resolves only after font loading and layout complete. Therefore the browser path must await fonts, measure after layout, and invalidate placement on reflow. References: https://www.w3.org/TR/cssom-view/ and https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FontFaceSet/ready . CSS Paged Media supplies the conceptual page-box and margin model, but it remains a browser layout contract rather than proof of reproducible pagination: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-page-3/ .

C3: Atlas and Codex need shared semantic view state, not merely synchronized event handlers.

Selection, focus references, epistemic horizon, active relation layers, comparison policy, feature derivation, uncertainty policy, and audit trail should live in CommonViewState. AtlasSpec adds projection, camera, and level of detail. CodexSpec adds reading mode, pagination, and annotation-lane policy. Both compilers consume the same semantic selection and visibility result. Then Codex to Atlas synchronization is true by construction.

C4: one semantic annotation, many placed fragments.

TextAnnotation should carry one stable AnnotationId, a typed target address, support SpanSet, status, priority, and AuditTrail. Avoid parallel optional claim and evidence fields that can disagree. Pagination derives FragmentIds from AnnotationId plus page and line fragment. Selection targets AnnotationId, so reflow can replace every rectangle without changing identity.

C5: do not create a second relation ontology for hyperlinks.

The proposed SemanticLink enum overlaps story relations, ProjectionMode, document identity, claim evidence, and later alignment types. SameEntity, Before, Causes, SummaryOf, and RetrospectiveReference must be projections of existing domain values. Portal, preview card, local arc, and split view are rendering topologies. They are not new facts.

C6: the scale control is a recipe selector, not one scalar axis.

Word, clause, sentence, three sentences, event, scene, and episode are different aggregation bases, some surface-based and some model-based. Present them as named FeatureDerivation recipes with declared window, reducer, coverage, and normalization. Only interpolate within a compatible kernel family. Events must become a real WindowBasis before the UI offers event aggregation.

C7: overlapping windows cannot be encoded by stacking translucent rectangles.

Alpha composition would make opacity depend on how many windows overlap rather than on the declared value. Render one resampled scalar field over the source axis with an explicit sampling rule, or render one selected window exactly. Coverage and missingness require a separate mask. Every aggregate also needs a visible circularity badge or warning derived from FeatureUseLedger.

C8: the annotation grammar needs lane ownership and collision laws.

Underline currently means local semantic unit, proposition, or event support. Hatching means uncertainty or model disagreement. A right gutter may simultaneously want entities, places, goals, temporal links, causal links, and recall. The compiler should allocate typed lanes under a lens-specific channel budget, reject or summarize incompatible combinations, and give selected marks priority. This is a semantic constraint, not just label collision avoidance.

C9: context membership is not always a contiguous textual scope.

A ContextFrame can have discontinuous support, and a proposition can belong to a speech or belief context even when the lexical cue lies elsewhere. Side bands should distinguish exact scope evidence, contextual membership, and inferred continuation. A solid contiguous band must never be synthesized from the hull of a discontinuous SpanSet.

C10: continuity threads can accidentally assert unsupported presence.

Connecting entity mentions through a gap, showing an entity as active but unnamed, or placing active character and location in the page header all make state claims. Render mention continuity directly. Render latent presence or relationship state only when a typed accepted claim supports it, with its status visible. Uncertain coreference is an alternative identity structure, not merely a dotted line style.

C11: exact text needs a DOM round-trip law.

The canonical DOM text-node concatenation must equal canonicalText exactly. Build an explicit map from the existing zero-based half-open UTF-16 offsets to DOM Range fragments. At compilation, reject spans that split a surrogate pair or violate the selected grapheme policy. Token wrappers must not insert textual whitespace or punctuation. DOM selection back to TextSpan and TextSpan to DOM rectangles should round-trip under randomized Unicode fixtures.

C12: reproducible pages need a layout receipt distinct from a view receipt.

Record font asset hashes, fallback resolution, shaping and pagination engine version, page dimensions, margins, line height, hyphenation and language policy, and relevant viewport or device parameters. Reflow mode guarantees stable semantic identity, not stable pages. Fixed edition mode guarantees stable pages only under a fully specified layout backend.

C13: cross-page continuation is a first-class fragmentation model.

Scene brackets, context bands, feature windows, and discontinuous evidence may all fragment across pages. Each fragment points to its semantic annotation and declares start, continuation, end, or portal. Page portals must not imply that the underlying relation itself is a portal.

C14: page carpet geometry needs its own projection contract.

Discourse ordering is meaningful. Row breaks, page adjacency in the second dimension, and thumbnail distance are layout conveniences unless explicitly declared otherwise. The page carpet should state that clearly, just as the Atlas does.

C15: keep AMR and proposition arcs aggressively local.

Inline arcs work for one line or a small selected clause. Cross-line roles, reentrancy over distant spans, embedded contexts, and cross-page relations should move to a proposition card or portal. Otherwise the canonical reading view turns into the graph viewer we are trying to avoid.

C16: revised first vertical slice.

1. Exact selectable DOM source with source-offset round trips.
2. Pure CodexFlow compiler and inspectable static HTML artifact.
3. One fixed edition PaginationSpec plus continuous-scroll layout.
4. Event, scene, and episode fragments only from validated data.
5. One feature derivation with scale recipes, coverage, missingness, and circularity audit.
6. Entity mention navigation without unsupported between-mention presence.
7. Claim and proposition inspector with local evidence highlighting.
8. Reader-horizon build versus omniscient build.
9. One typed nonlocal relation rendered as paired portal tabs.
10. Saved CommonViewState plus Codex, layout, and model receipts.

For War of the Ghosts, exact source and available feature tracks may render immediately. Narrative annotations must come from the explicitly labeled researcher-reviewed narrative acceptance fixture or a validated acquired model. The Codex should never fill a spectacular demo by inventing missing structure.

Role for Intaglio

Intaglio is well suited to the SVG annotation overlay and export path if its keyed graphics can support stable AnnotationId groups, bounds, transforms, clipping, hit testing, and lane geometry. It should not own canonical text, pagination truth, DOM selection, model semantics, or inference. The Canvas scalar field is a later measured optimization. This dogfood target is valuable precisely because it exposes which graphics mechanisms are genuinely reusable without forcing story concepts into Intaglio.
